chunks: Ahmad narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "Hajj is obligatory upon the man even if he has a debt."
ai.seo_question: Is Hajj obligatory if I have unpaid debts?
ai.summary: In the Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith clarifies that Hajj is obligatory even for those with debts, provided they have sufficient wealth to settle the debt or can do so during the pilgrimage. This ruling emphasizes that the divine command is not suspended by financial obligations, distinguishing it from the condition of 'ability' (istita'ah) which requires net wealth after debts. The implication is that the debtor must prioritize settling creditors or ensure their consent, but the ritual duty remains active.
